h: From the Castle Esplanade to the Foul Line
p: Edinburgh is one of those cities where you can walk for hours and still feel like you've barely scratched the surface. For a cracking view before your game, climb Calton Hill at the end of Princes Street; it's an easy short climb with monuments dotted across the top and sweeping views over the city and out to the Firth of Forth. Arthur's Seat is the bigger challenge if your legs are up to it.

The National Museum of Scotland on Chambers Street is free and could fill a whole afternoon, while the Scottish National Gallery at the foot of the Mound is another free treat. For something quieter, follow the Water of Leith walkway down to Dean Village, a picture-perfect cluster of old buildings by the river that feels a world away from the city bustle. Down in Leith, the waterfront is a lively spot for food and drink.

At the lanes, a few things help everyone have a better time. Sort out teams before you start so there's no debating after the first frame, and if you've got complete beginners, pair them with someone who's bowled before. Don't grab the heaviest ball; choose one you can swing smoothly and control. Aim for the arrows painted on the lane rather than the pins themselves, and keep your arm straight on the follow-through.
Getting about is easy, with trams, buses and Waverley Station keeping the city well connected, so leave the car at the hotel and enjoy the evening.
